data.body: Follow-up of DX-reviewer-independence-soft (rules.py was held by repair-drv). (1) completion/rules.py: _independence/verdict add ONE neutral warning when GR.tier_notes(item, gdefs) is non-empty (`v.warnings += ...`); needs_independent_reviewer keeps reading the legacy boolean, which already composes with independence_level (level off passes in independence_tier). Complete-time enforcement already goes through G.reviewer_independence, so the knob and tier fallback are live at complete without this. If rules.py would pass 30000 bytes, split the independence helpers into completion/independence.py. (2) `ddflow reviewers detect` and setup: detect which models the account can reach and propose a reviewer set of DIFFERENT models of the one family, saying so plainly; one reachable model only => gate unavailable. (3) metrics: confirmed findings per review by tier (the `tier` group-by dimension and recorded independence_tier exist; add confirmed-finding counts). (4) the picker orders by family then distance; consider reachability-based fallback accounting.
data.title: Complete prints the independence tier note once; setup/reviewers propose a same-family reviewer set; confirmed findings per tier

data.claim: completion/rules.py::_independence calls G.reviewer_independence, so tier logic inside it governs complete
data.falsifier: a complete refusal that bypasses reviewer_independence
data.mechanism: single call site at rules.py:254 returns (ok, why)
data.probe_output: ddflow/services/completion/rules.py:254 is the only non-test caller
data.question: Does the existing shared check decide completion, so a tier added there changes complete without editing rules.py?

evidence.note: research note CONFIRMED: rules.py:254 is the only caller of reviewer_independence

r-reuse-core: one check (independence_tier) extended in reviewers.py; r-small-files: reviewers.py 22.6KB, new tier.py; r-everything-configurable: agent.reviewer_independence knob; r-no-shell: nothing needs a shell
commit 4faa4dbd5; tests/test_reviewer_independence_soft.py 11 passed; related suites pass except the baseline-red architecture guards

chunk_findings.detail: The change breaks the previous invariant that the selection message is based on the reviewers actually used. Before, `revs = selected.reviewers`, so `_say_selection(selected, say)` necessarily described the final reviewer set. Now `revs` is the filtered/ordered result of `_prefer_independent`, but `_say_selection` is still called with the original `selected` object. If `prefer_independent` returns a new list (the natural sort/filter implementation, and the reason the call site assigns its return value), a reviewer that is dropped by the hard floor or reordered away is still announced as selected. For example, with configured reviewers `[author_model, same_family_other_model]`, `dispatch.select` may return both, `_say_selection` says the author model was selected, while `revs` excludes it and it never runs. This violates tell-dont-discover and can make any consumer of `selected.reviewers` (status/metrics/fallback reporting) disagree with the review that actually ran.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/review/run.py:394 (`revs = _prefer_independent(...)`)

chunk_findings.detail: `author = cfg.agent.family or open_session_model(st, agent)` makes a configured `[agent].family` override the author’s known session model. If this project sets `[agent].family = "anthropic"` while the current session model is `claude-3-5-sonnet`, a review by `claude-3-5-sonnet` calls `GR.review_tier(cfg, "anthropic", "claude-3-5-sonnet", "anthropic")`. The tier function receives only the family string as the author, not the author model, so it cannot apply the “author’s own model never counts” floor; it will classify the same-model review as the same-family `model` tier instead of `none`. That lets the author’s own model satisfy a model-tier gate and makes gate evidence/status report independence that should be refused.
chunk_findings.title: `ddflow/api/review/tier.py:16`

chunk_findings.detail: The same family-over-session-model choice is used for picker ordering, so within-family fallback does not actually prefer the model farthest from the author. With `[agent].family = "anthropic"` and session model `claude-3-5-sonnet`, `_distance` compares `"anthropic"` to candidate model ids. For `claude-3-5-haiku` and `claude-3-7-opus`, both distances from `"anthropic"` are 5, so the stable sort preserves config order. If `haiku` is configured first, the picker chooses `haiku`, not the model farther from the author’s actual model (`opus` is distance 4 from `sonnet`, `haiku` is distance 3), violating the operator clarification that same-family fallback should prefer the farthest model (different generation/tier).
chunk_findings.title: `ddflow/api/review/tier.py:39`

chunk_findings.detail: `reviewed = [r for r in (results or [best]) if r.status <= best.status] or [best]` counts unavailable outcomes when the best outcome is unavailable. If every reviewer attempt is unavailable, each result has the same unavailable status as `best`, so the filter keeps them and `GR.review_tier` is called on their configured model/family. The returned evidence can be `independence_tier: family` or `model` even though no review actually ran. The gate tier should be none/unavailable in that case; a review that could not run is unavailable, never passed.
chunk_findings.title: `ddflow/api/review/tier.py:20`

chunk_findings.detail: `review_tier` treats a non-empty reviewer model string as a recognised, different model as soon as a family is supplied, and it decides “same model” only by lower-casing the raw strings. For example, with `author_model="anthropic/claude-3-5-sonnet"`, `rev_model="claude-3-5-sonnet"`, and `rev_family="anthropic"`, the two model ids are the same model with a provider prefix, but `m != a`, the family matches, and the function returns `model`; the gate then accepts the author’s own model as the fallback, violating the hard floor that the author’s own model never counts. The same code path also returns `model` for `rev_model="not-a-known-model"` with `rev_family="anthropic"`, because it never checks that the reviewer model itself is recognised, contradicting “unrecognised models establish nothing.”
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/gates/reviewers.py:review_tier

chunk_findings.detail: The new rule text says `ddflow complete` refuses a review with no tier even though the same parenthetical says `[agent].reviewer_independence = off` demands none. For a project with `agent.reviewer_independence = off`, a review with no recognized tier should not be rejected on independence grounds (subject to the separate author-model floor), but the driver instruction tells agents it will be refused; following it, an agent will either invent a tier or treat a valid off-mode review as failing. The same contradictory sentence is duplicated in `docs/ddflow/drivers/implement-phase.md`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/drivers/implement-phase.md:178

chunk_findings.detail: The test requires `prefer_independent` to return the author's own model as the last candidate (`got[-1] == "claude-opus-5"`). The hard floor in D-reviewer-independence-soft-why says the author's own model never reviews/counts and, if only that model is reachable, the gate must be recorded unavailable. If the picker is used as a preference list and a caller selects the first available reviewer, a configuration where the author model is the only configured/reachable reviewer will still receive that model from `prefer_independent` and can run the review instead of being refused. The test should assert that the author model is absent from the independent reviewer list.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_reviewer_independence_soft.py:test_the_picker_prefers_another_family_then_the_farthest_model

chunk_findings.detail: The test only checks that the note contains `tier model`, has length one, and lacks the literal substring `must`. It does not enforce the operator requirement that tier-model output is neutral and is a hint rather than a warning. A `tier_notes` implementation returning `["WARNING: tier model review; run ddflow review --reviewer ..."]` would satisfy this test while violating D-reviewer-independence-soft-why.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_reviewer_independence_soft.py:test_tier_notes_are_neutral_and_once

chunk_findings.detail: When `[agent].family` is configured, both `_tier_evidence` and `prefer_independent` set `author` to only the family string and discard the concrete session model returned by `open_session_model(st, agent)`. This makes the author's own model impossible to identify later. Concrete example: `cfg.agent.family = "anthropic"`, the agent's own model is `anthropic/claude-opus-4-1`, and reviewers are configured in order `[anthropic/claude-opus-4-1, anthropic/claude-haiku-3-5]`. `prefer_independent` passes `author="anthropic"` to `GR.review_tier`, so both reviewers are judged as same-family `"model"` tier, and `_distance("anthropic", "anthropic/claude-opus-4-1")` and `_distance("anthropic", "anthropic/claude-haiku-3-5")` are both 4; the stable sort leaves the author's own model first instead of last. The picker can therefore select the author's own model as reviewer, and `_tier_evidence` records an own-model passing review as tier `"model"` rather than `"none"`, violating the hard floor in D-reviewer-independence-soft that the author's own model never counts.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/review/tier.py:16,39

chunk_findings.detail: The reviewer independence gate does not use the configured `[agent].reviewer_independence` level at all. It returns `tier != "none"` unconditionally. With the knob set to `family` (the strictest level), a review that reached tier `model` (same family, different model) will satisfy the check because `"model" != "none"` is True, defeating the requirement that a different pretraining family is needed. Conversely, with the knob set to `off`, the function will still return False when no tier can be established (for example, no reviewer or an unknown model), incorrectly enforcing independence when the feature is disabled. The docstring explicitly says “Level `family` reports a same-family panel unsatisfied even when every reviewer passed,” but the implementation does the opposite.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/gates/reviewers.py:check_independence

chunk_findings.detail: The updated implement-phase rule says unconditionally that “`ddflow complete` refuses a review with no tier,” but this same change’s upgrade note in `ddflow/templates/upgrade/unreleased/knob_added.agent.reviewer_independence.toml` says `agent.reviewer_independence = "off"` “demands none.” A project that sets `off` is therefore given contradictory instructions: the managed rule tells the implement-phase agent that a tier is required, while the knob says none is required. The template/doc should exempt `off`, e.g. “when `family` or `model` is selected.”
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/drivers/implement-phase.md:177 and docs/ddflow/drivers/implement-phase.md:177

chunk_findings.detail: `_say_selection(selected, say)` is still called with the pre-filtered `selected` object even though the reviewers that will actually run are `revs = _prefer_independent(...)`. Because the hard floor says the author’s own model never reviews, `_prefer_independent` must be able to drop a reviewer from `selected.reviewers`; e.g. if the dispatch selected the author’s model plus a same-family fallback, the author model is removed and only the fallback is used, but `_say_selection` still announces the original selection. The operator is told a reviewer was selected that was not used (or, in the author-only case, is told a selection was made immediately before the gate is recorded unavailable), violating the “tell, don’t discover” requirement.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/review/run.py:395

chunk_findings.detail: `author = cfg.agent.family or open_session_model(st, agent)` makes `author` a family string whenever `[agent].family` is configured, but that value is then used as a model id in `_distance` (line 45). This breaks the picker’s “farthest model from the author” rule. For example, with `[agent].family = "anthropic"` and the author’s session model `"claude-3-5-sonnet"`, candidate `"claude-3-5-sonnet-1"` has `_distance("anthropic", ...) == 6`, while genuinely farther `"claude-4-opus"` has distance `4`; because the key uses `-distance`, the near model is sorted ahead of the far model. The same conflation also prevents the author model from having distance `0`, so the documented “author’s own model last” behavior can fail when the tier check treats same-family models as tier `model`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/review/tier.py:16

chunk_findings.detail: The managed-instruction text hard-codes that “a different model of the same family is accepted, recorded as tier `model`”, but `independence_level` in `ddflow/config_sections/agent.py` can return `family` when `[agent].reviewer_independence = "family"` or that value is org-locked. In a family-locked organisation, an agent following this generated rule will submit a same-family, different-model reviewer, while the gate’s effective independence level is `family` and will reject it; the rule text is wrong for that valid configuration and should be conditional on the configured level or omit the fallback when family is enforced.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/adopt/_rules.py:61

chunk_findings.detail: `review_tier` treats any non-empty reviewer string as a model id as long as its family resolves; it only rejects a *bare family author*, not a bare family reviewer. With a recognised family `anthropic`, a call like `review_tier(cfg, "claude-3.5-sonnet", "anthropic", "anthropic")` has `routed is None`, `author_fam == "anthropic"`, `fam == "anthropic"`, `m == "anthropic"`, `a == "claude-3.5-sonnet"`, and `bare is False`, so it returns `"model"`. That records a same-family model-tier review even though `"anthropic"` is a family alias, not a distinct model id, contrary to D-reviewer-independence-soft: a model-tier review requires a different model, and an unrecognised/non-model string should establish nothing.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/gates/reviewers.py:review_tier

chunk_findings.detail: `model_tier_of` falls back to `rec.by` when the gate evidence has no `model` field: `rec.evidence.get("model", rec.by)`. `rec.by` is the reviewer name (the trust message in `_no_reviewer_refusal` calls it “reviewer”), not necessarily a model. Given a gate record with `by="anthropic"` and empty evidence, and `fams=[("rubber_duck", "anthropic")]` while `author_model="claude-3.5-sonnet"`, `model_tier_of` computes `m="anthropic"` and returns `"anthropic"` because `review_tier` accepts the family alias as a model-tier model. This can report a model-tier review from a reviewer name/missing model evidence, violating “unrecognised models establish nothing” and “model tier = same family, a different model id”.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/gates/reviewers.py:model_tier_of

chunk_findings.detail: With `[agent].reviewer_independence = "off"`, `independence_tier` returns `("off", ...)` before it checks the author identity, reviewer models, or whether any reviewer ran. For an item whose only reviewer ran with the same model as the author, this returns a non-`none` tier instead of `none`, so any shared gate logic that treats a tier other than `none` as “usable/independent” (or records it as evidence) will count the author’s own model as a reviewer. That violates the stated hard floor that the author’s own model never counts; the `off` branch should still apply the author/no-reviewer refusals, or `off` must not be returned as a tier.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/gates/reviewers.py:independence_tier

chunk_findings.detail: The test requires `prefer_independent` to return the author's own model as a picked reviewer candidate (`got[-1] == "claude-opus-5"`). The change's hard floor is explicit: the author's own model never reviews. A reviewer picker that includes the author model in its returned list makes it selectable; if the other three candidates are unavailable, this ordering still yields the author model instead of an empty/unavailable picker result, enabling self-review.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_reviewer_independence_soft.py:test_the_picker_prefers_another_family_then_the_farthest_model

chunk_findings.detail: `_say_selection(selected, say)` is called after `revs = _prefer_independent(...)`, but it still receives the original `selected` object rather than a copy updated with the actual `revs`. If `_prefer_independent` returns a different list (e.g., it reorders reviewers to put different-family first or removes the author’s own model under the hard floor), the operator-facing selection message reports reviewers that will not run. Example: `selected.reviewers = [author-model, other-model]` and the policy says the author’s own model never reviews; `_prefer_independent` returns `[other-model]`, but `_say_selection` reports both were selected, contradicting the recorded tier evidence and the later gate status notes.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/review/run.py:391-393

chunk_findings.detail: The documented rule says “The author's own model never counts,” but the intended and enforced behavior is that the author’s own model never reviews. This understates the floor: an agent following the instruction could select the author’s model as a reviewer, assuming the system will merely not count it, while the safe behavior is to refuse to run it. The rule text should say the author’s own model is never used as a reviewer.
chunk_findings.title: AGENTS.md:26, CLAUDE.md:26

chunk_findings.detail: `author` is chosen as `cfg.agent.family` first, discarding the actual session model. Thus whenever `[agent].family` is set (the normal configuration for the independence knob), a bare family label such as `"anthropic"` is passed to `GR.review_tier` and `_distance`. The author's exact model is no longer available there, so the author's own model cannot be distinguished from a different model of that family. Example: session model is `"claude-opus-4-5"`, `cfg.agent.family = "anthropic"`, and the reviewer list contains `"claude-opus-4-5"`; the picker ranks that reviewer as a same-family model rather than `none`/last, and `_tier_evidence` can record `{"independence_tier": "model"}` for the author's own model. This violates the hard floor “the author own model never counts” from D-reviewer-independence-soft, and the intended “farthest model from the author” preference is not computed from the author model.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/review/tier.py:16 and tier.py:39

chunk_findings.detail: The new `reviewer_independence` knob documentation says “The legacy boolean `reviewer_family_must_differ = false` still means `off`,” but `independence_level` returns `"family"` whenever `agent.reviewer_independence == "family"`, even when `agent.reviewer_family_must_differ` is `False`. For example, a project config with `reviewer_independence = "family"` and a local `reviewer_family_must_differ = false` still gets `"family"`, so the legacy off switch has no effect and a different-family reviewer is still required. Either the function must let the legacy false force `"off"`, or the knob/function documentation must say that any `"family"` setting outranks the legacy false flag.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/config_sections/agent.py:independence_level

chunk_findings.detail: The function never checks that the reviewer’s family is actually a recognised family in `cfg.agent.families`. With an approved reviewer record whose declared `family` is `"not-a-known-family"` and an unknown model id, `_declared_family(...)` returns that raw string, `fam` is nonempty, and `fam not in [author_fam]` returns `"family"`. That makes a nonexistent family satisfy the strictest family tier, contrary to the function’s own contract that an unrecognised reviewer family establishes nothing.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/gates/reviewers.py review_tier

chunk_findings.detail: `review_tier` returns `"family"` before applying the bare-family-author guard. Given `author_model="anthropic"` (a bare family name), `rev_model="gpt-4"`, and a config where `anthropic` and `openai` are family names, `_author_identity` supplies `author_fam="anthropic"`; the call then hits `if fam not in [author_fam]: return "family"` before `bare = bool(family_name_of(...))` is evaluated. The old code refused this via `_author_no_identity_refusal`, and the new docstring says an author that is a bare family establishes nothing, so this should be `"none"`, not `"family"`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/gates/reviewers.py review_tier

chunk_findings.detail: The hunk converts the `not fams` early returns from `False, ...` to a bare string because the new caller does `if why := _no_reviewer_refusal(...): return "none", why`. But the earlier `if unapproved:` early return whose closing `)` is the first context line of the hunk is left unchanged and still returns `(False, msg)`. For an item where `_reviewer_fams` returns a nonempty `unapproved` list, `why` becomes `(False, "...")`, which is truthy, so `independence_tier` returns `("none", (False, "..."))` instead of `("none", "...")`, violating its `tuple[str, str]` contract and breaking any consumer that expects a string explanation.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/gates/reviewers.py `_no_reviewer_refusal` unapproved branch

chunk_findings.detail: `prefer_independent` identifies the author's own model by exact lowercased string equality (`r.model.strip().lower() != author.strip().lower()`). Model ids are not necessarily canonical: the author's session model may include a provider prefix or a different punctuation/date form, while a reviewer entry may name the same model without that prefix. For example, if the author session model is `anthropic/claude-opus-4-1` and a reviewer is configured with `model="claude-opus-4-1"` and `family="anthropic"`, the filter keeps that reviewer as a candidate. A caller that uses the first returned reviewer can therefore select the author's own model, violating the hard floor that the author's own model never reviews/counts.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/review/tier.py:60

chunk_findings.detail: `return others or ordered` returns the author's own model when every candidate is the author model. For `revs=[Review(model="claude-opus-5", family="anthropic")]` and session model `claude-opus-5`, `others` is empty, so `prefer_independent` returns `[Review(model="claude-opus-5")]`. A picker/caller that treats the returned list as available reviewers will run the author model even though, with only the author model reachable, the gate should be recorded unavailable and never passed.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/review/tier.py:61

chunk_findings.detail: `reviewer_family_must_differ=false` is mapped to `off`, but then it is allowed to override an explicit `reviewer_independence="model"` while an explicit `reviewer_independence="family"` is not. Since `model` is stricter than `off` (`model` demands a different model; `off` demands no independence), the function’s stated “strictest wins” rule is not implemented for the `model` level. A project with `[agent] reviewer_family_must_differ=false` and `[agent] reviewer_independence="model"` gets `independence_level()` -> `"off"`, so the gate will not require the different-model review the new knob asked for. This is a concrete failure of the new knob: the legacy boolean silently weakens an explicit `model` request, but not an explicit `family` request, producing inconsistent effective independence levels for contradictory settings.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/config_sections/agent.py:independence_level

chunk_findings.detail: `check_independence` now computes `tier, why = independence_tier(...)` and returns `tier != "none"`, but it never compares that tier to `[agent].reviewer_independence` / `independence_level(cfg)`. With `[agent].reviewer_independence = "family"` (including an org-locked family setting), a passing reviewer from the author’s family but a different model produces `tier == "model"`, so `check_independence` returns `True` and the gate accepts the fallback that the knob is supposed to refuse. Conversely, with `[agent].reviewer_independence = "off"`, a review with no recognized tier has `tier == "none"`, so the function returns `False` even though independence should be disabled.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/gates/reviewers.py:check_independence

chunk_findings.detail: `tier_notes` emits the “reviewed within the author's model family” note whenever any recorded reviewer gate has `independence_tier == "model"`, without checking whether another passing reviewer achieved `independence_tier == "family"`. For example, if the author is `anthropic/claude-opus` and the item has both `critic` by `anthropic/claude-haiku` with tier `model` and `roborev` by `openai/gpt-4` with tier `family`, `tier_notes` still returns a note saying the review was within the author’s model family and suggesting a cross-family reviewer, even though a cross-family review already exists.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/gates/reviewers.py:tier_notes

chunk_findings.detail: When `[agent].reviewer_independence = "off"`, `independence_tier` immediately returns `("off", "reviewer independence is off ...")` before it looks up the item, resolves the author identity, or inspects any reviewer outcome. A gate that records this tier as the independence evidence (and the new `independence_tier` field is exactly that evidence) can therefore see a non-`none` tier for an item with no reviewer outcome or with only the author's own model. That contradicts the hard floor in D-reviewer-independence-soft-why: the author's own model must never count, and a review that could not run is unavailable, not passed. It also conflicts with the new metrics field in `ddflow/services/metrics/facts.py:46`, which documents tier as only `family | model | none`, so an `off` tier is outside the stated evidence domain and can be misbucketed by tier-based metrics.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/gates/reviewers.py:303 (`independence_tier`)

chunk_findings.detail: The newly changed enforcement sentence says `ddflow complete` refuses a review with no tier unless the level is `off`. That is not the correct rule for the strict `family` level. For a project with `[agent].reviewer_independence = family` and a same-family different-model reviewer, the review outcome has a tier (`model`), so the documented sentence says it is not refused, while the same paragraph and the intent say `family` has no fallback and must refuse the model tier. The managed rule should say that completion refuses a review whose tier is below the configured level (`family` requires `family`; `model` requires `model` or `family`; `off` demands none, still with the author-model floor), not merely a review with no tier.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/drivers/implement-phase.md:178 (and docs/ddflow/drivers/implement-phase.md:179)

chunk_findings.detail: The test is the only check for the user-facing tier-model note, but it verifies only that there is one note, that it contains `"tier model"` and `"Hint"`, and that it lacks a few banned words. The operator requirement for this change says the tier-model output must name which models reviewed and give the exact way to get a family review. An implementation returning, for example, `["Hint: tier model review; run ddflow review --reviewer <configured-reviewer>"]` or `["Hint: tier model review; see ddflow review --reviewer"]` passes this test even though it does not name the reviewer model(s) that ran or the configured reviewers. Thus the test gives false confidence that the required tell-dont-discover output is present. [D-reviewer-independence-soft-why] [r-tell-dont-discover]
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_reviewer_independence_soft.py:test_tier_notes_are_neutral_and_once

chunk_findings.detail: The implementation contradicts the documented mapping for the legacy boolean. Both the knob doc (`reviewer_family_must_differ = false` still means `off`) and the function’s own docstring say `off` when the legacy boolean is false, but the first branch `if agent.reviewer_independence == "family": return "family"` runs before that check. Given `agent.reviewer_family_must_differ = False` and `agent.reviewer_independence = "family"` (for example an org-locked family setting), `independence_level(agent)` returns `"family"`, not `"off"`. Downstream gates then still require a different pretraining family, so a project that disabled the legacy requirement cannot actually turn the independence requirement off as documented.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/config_sections/agent.py:independence_level

chunk_findings.detail: The gate decision is just `tier != "none"`; it never compares `cfg.agent.reviewer_independence` / `independence_level`. With `[agent].reviewer_independence = "family"`, a review whose `independence_tier` is `"model"` (same family, different model) returns satisfied, defeating the strictest setting. With `[agent].reviewer_independence = "off"`, a review whose tier is `"none"` returns unsatisfied even though `off` demands no independence tier. The configured knob therefore does not control this check. [D-reviewer-independence-soft]
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/gates/reviewers.py:check_independence

chunk_findings.detail: The `level == "off"` branch returns `("off", ...)` before `_reviewer_fams` or `model_tier_of` ever run, so the one shared independence check never applies the hard floor that the author's own model never counts. With `[agent].reviewer_independence = "off"` and a review recorded by the author's own model (for example author `claude-opus-4-1` with `--reviewer claude-opus-4-1`), this function returns tier `"off"` rather than `"none"`; the gate then has no independence-based reason to mark the review unavailable, violating D-reviewer-independence-soft-why (e): the author own model never counts, and with only that model reachable the gate must be unavailable, never passed.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/gates/reviewers.py:independence_tier

chunk_findings.detail: The rule text says unconditionally: “When none is available, a different MODEL of your family also satisfies the gate”, then in the same sentence says “at `family` there is no fallback”. With `[agent].reviewer_independence = family`, a same-family different model does **not** satisfy the gate, so an implement-phase agent can follow the main clause, pick a same-family reviewer, and have `ddflow complete` refuse the gate. The last clause also only says complete refuses “a review with no tier”, omitting that at `family` a tier-`model` review is insufficient. The model fallback should be stated as applying only at level `model` (the default), not as a general rule.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/drivers/implement-phase.md:175-178, docs/ddflow/drivers/implement-phase.md:175-178

chunk_findings.detail: The new assertion still does not enforce the operator clarification’s “no urgency wording” requirement from D-reviewer-independence-soft-why. It only rejects the literal substrings `must`, `warning`, and `refus`; a `tier_notes` implementation returning `["Hint: urgent tier model; run ddflow review --reviewer ..."]` passes every assertion (length 1, contains `Hint` and `tier model`, none of the blocked substrings) while still using urgency wording, so the test gives false confidence that the neutrality requirement is enforced.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_reviewer_independence_soft.py:test_tier_notes_are_neutral_and_once

chunk_findings.detail: When every candidate reviewer is the author's own model, `others` is empty and the function returns `ordered`, which still contains the author's model. For example, with `open_session_model(...) == "claude-opus-5"` and `revs=[Reviewer(model="claude-opus-5")]`, `prefer_independent` returns `[Reviewer(model="claude-opus-5")]`. A caller that dispatches the picker's result will run the author's own model, violating the hard floor in [D-reviewer-independence-soft] that the author's own model never reviews and that a one-model situation should be unavailable rather than usable. This is the same gap as previous finding 7, still present in the new `return others or ordered` line.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/review/tier.py:61 (`prefer_independent`)

chunk_findings.detail: `reviewed = [r for r in (results or [best]) if ...]` conflates an empty `results` list with `None`. If a caller passes `results=[]` to mean “no review outcomes”, but `best` is a reviewed family-tier result, the function ignores the empty result set and returns `{"independence_tier": "family"}` from `best`. That records a gate tier based on a review outside the supplied result set, contrary to the evidence rule that a review that could not run is unavailable and that the gate tier is the best among the passing reviewers [D-reviewer-independence-soft]. The fallback should be `results if results is not None else [best]`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/review/tier.py:28 (`_tier_evidence`)

chunk_findings.detail: The new helper contradicts its own documented contract. Both the knob docs and the function docstring say that legacy `reviewer_family_must_differ = false` means `off`, but the implementation returns `"family"` first whenever `reviewer_independence == "family"`, before checking the legacy boolean. Concrete input: `[agent] reviewer_independence = "family"` and `reviewer_family_must_differ = false`. The documented/effective-off behavior is overridden: `independence_level()` returns `"family"`, so a same-family different-model reviewer is refused even though the legacy off switch is supposed to disable independence. This makes the legacy boolean unreliable and the user-facing rule text wrong.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/config_sections/agent.py:independence_level

chunk_findings.detail: `review_tier` accepts a declared reviewer family without checking that it is one of the configured families. The value is taken from `_declared_family({"reviewer": "x", "family": rev_family})` and is only rejected when it is empty or when it equals the author family. With `author_model="claude-3.5-sonnet"` (author family `anthropic`), a call such as `review_tier(cfg, "claude-3.5-sonnet", "x", "not-a-known-family")` returns `"family"` because `"not-a-known-family" not in ["anthropic"]`. That lets a fabricated or unrecognised family satisfy the strictest family tier, contrary to the function’s own contract and D-reviewer-independence-soft.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/gates/reviewers.py:review_tier

chunk_findings.detail: `review_tier` treats any non-empty reviewer string as a model once the family resolves; it only rejects an exact model-id match. For example, with `author_model="claude-3.5-sonnet"`, `review_tier(cfg, "claude-3.5-sonnet", "not-a-model", "anthropic")` returns `"model"`: the family is the author’s family, `m="not-a-model"`, `a="claude-3.5-sonnet"`, `m != a`, and the author is not a bare family. This records a model-tier review for an unrecognised model (or a bare family name used as a model), while the change says unrecognised models establish nothing. Previous finding 4 still holds.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/gates/reviewers.py:review_tier

chunk_findings.detail: The family return is evaluated before the bare-author guard. If the author model is a bare family, e.g. `review_tier(cfg, "anthropic", "gpt-4", "openai")`, `_author_identity` supplies `author_fam="anthropic"`, the reviewer family `"openai"` is outside `[author_fam]`, and the function returns `"family"` before computing `bare = bool(family_name_of(author_model, cfg.agent.families))`. The docstring says a bare-family author establishes nothing, so this should return `"none"` because the exact author model is unknown. Previous finding 13 still holds.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/gates/reviewers.py:review_tier

chunk_findings.detail: `model_tier_of` uses `rec.by` as a fallback model: `rec.evidence.get("model", rec.by)`. If a gate record has no `model` evidence and `by="rubber_duck"` (a reviewer name), with `fams=[("rubber_duck", "anthropic")]` and `author_model="claude-3.5-sonnet"`, the function sets `m="rubber_duck"`, accepts it as tier `model` via `review_tier`, and returns `"rubber_duck"` as the reviewer model. That records a reviewer identity, not a model, as the model that achieved tier `model`, corrupting the evidence used for metrics and hints. Previous finding 5 still holds.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/gates/reviewers.py:model_tier_of

chunk_findings.detail: The hunk changes the `not fams` refusals to plain strings so `independence_tier` can do `if why := _no_reviewer_refusal(...)`, but the preceding unapproved-reviewer return is still the old `(False, msg)` tuple (its closing `)` is the unchanged context line). Given an item whose reviewer is unapproved, `_reviewer_fams` returns a non-empty `unapproved`, `_no_reviewer_refusal` returns a truthy tuple, and `independence_tier` returns `("none", (False, "..."))` instead of `("none", "...")`. This breaks the declared `tuple[str, str]` contract and makes the refusal explanation a tuple, so any caller that formats or slices the explanation gets wrong output or fails. Previous finding 14 still applies.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/gates/reviewers.py:_no_reviewer_refusal

chunk_findings.detail: The new `level == "off"` early return bypasses the item lookup, reviewer evidence, author identity, and the hard floor. With `[agent].reviewer_independence = "off"`, a nonexistent item, an item with no reviewer, or an item whose only reviewer used the author's own model returns `("off", ...)` rather than `("none", ...)`. The docstring and D-reviewer-independence-soft hard floor require the author's own model never to count and a review that could not run to be unavailable, not passed; any gate logic that treats a non-`none` tier as usable evidence will record self-review or a missing review as `off`. Previous finding 6 still applies.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/gates/reviewers.py:independence_tier

chunk_findings.detail: This test records a `critic` review by `"claude-opus-5"`, which is the author model used by `_tier`, then sets independence off (`reviewer_family_must_differ = False`) and asserts `independence_tier` returns `"off"`. The hard floor says the author's own model never counts and a same-model review must be `none`/unavailable regardless of the independence knob. As written, the test locks in a non-`none` result for a self-review; any gate logic that treats a returned tier other than `none` as usable evidence will accept the author's own model when independence is off. The off-level test should either use a non-author reviewer or assert `none` for the author model.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_reviewer_independence_soft.py:test_off_and_the_legacy_boolean (line 70)

chunk_findings.detail: `_distance` compares symmetric differences of all regex tokens equally, so a different-tier-only model ties with a different-generation model, even though the operator clarification requires the picker to prefer a different size or generation before a different tier. Example: author `"claude-3-sonnet"`; candidates `"claude-3-opus"` (same generation, different tier) and `"claude-2-sonnet"` (different generation, same tier) both get `_distance == 2`, so stable sorting preserves config order and can select the different-tier candidate over the different-generation candidate, violating the stated preference.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/review/tier.py:_distance

chunk_findings.detail: The function checks `agent.reviewer_independence == "family"` before `not agent.reviewer_family_must_differ`, so a config with `[agent].reviewer_independence = "family"` and the legacy `reviewer_family_must_differ = false` returns `"family"` instead of the documented `"off"`. The new knob doc explicitly says "The legacy boolean `reviewer_family_must_differ = false` still means `off`," and the function docstring says the same, so the legacy off switch is broken exactly when the newer family pin is present. Moving the legacy-false check before the family check (or correcting the docs to say family outranks false) would resolve the contradiction.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/config_sections/agent.py:independence_level

chunk_findings.detail: `review_tier` never verifies that the computed `fam` is a recognised family in `cfg.agent.families`. With `_declared_family(...)` returning the supplied family string, a nonexistent family still satisfies the strictest family tier: `review_tier(cfg, "claude-3.5-sonnet", "unknown-model", "not-a-known-family")` sets `fam = "not-a-known-family"`, `author_fam = "anthropic"`, then `fam not in [author_fam]` returns `"family"`. That contradicts the function's own contract that a reviewer whose family is not recognised establishes nothing, and lets an unknown/forged declared family pass a family-locked gate.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/gates/reviewers.py:review_tier

chunk_findings.detail: `review_tier` still accepts a bare family name as a reviewer model and records it as tier `model`. For `review_tier(cfg, "claude-3.5-sonnet", "anthropic", "anthropic")`, both `fam` and `m` are `"anthropic"`, `a` is `"claude-3.5-sonnet"`, the author is not bare, so the final return is `"model"` even though no different model of the same family was reviewed. The docstring requires a different model id, not just a family string, so this is still wrong.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/gates/reviewers.py:review_tier

chunk_findings.detail: The bare-family-author guard runs too late for a different-family reviewer. Given `author_model="anthropic"` (a recognised bare family), `rev_model="gpt-4"`, and `rev_family="openai"`, the code hits `if fam not in (routed if routed is not None else [author_fam])` and returns `"family"` before computing `bare = bool(family_name_of(author_model, cfg.agent.families))`. The contract says an author that is a bare family establishes nothing, so this must return `"none"`; instead it treats the review as fully cross-family.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/gates/reviewers.py:review_tier

chunk_findings.detail: `model_tier_of` falls back to `rec.by` when gate evidence has no `model` field: `m = str((rec.evidence.get("model", rec.by) if rec else "") or "").strip()`. `rec.by` is the reviewer name, not necessarily a model. For a gate record with `by="anthropic"`, empty evidence, `fams=[("rubber_duck", "anthropic")]`, and `author_model="claude-3.5-sonnet"`, this computes `m="anthropic"`, passes it to `review_tier`, and returns `"anthropic"` from `model_tier_of` because `review_tier` records a bare family as tier `model`. This can fabricate a recorded model review from reviewer metadata with no actual model id.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/gates/reviewers.py:model_tier_of

chunk_findings.detail: The unapproved-reviewer branch above this hunk still returns `(False, msg)`, while the branches changed here now return a bare string and `""`, so `_no_reviewer_refusal` has type `str | tuple[bool, str]`. `independence_tier` then does `if why := _no_reviewer_refusal(...): return "none", why`. For an item with an unapproved reviewer, `_reviewer_fams` returns a non-empty `unapproved` list; `_no_reviewer_refusal` returns `(False, "...")`, which is truthy, so `independence_tier` returns `("none", (False, "..."))` instead of a two-string tuple. This violates the `tuple[str, str]` contract and hands downstream callers a tuple where a string explanation is expected.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/gates/reviewers.py:_no_reviewer_refusal

chunk_findings.detail: At `level == "off"`, the function returns `("off", ...)` immediately, before the item is loaded or any reviewer model is checked. The hard floor in D-reviewer-independence-soft is that the author's own model never reviews/counts, but with `[agent].reviewer_independence = "off"` and author and reviewer both `"claude-opus"`, `independence_tier` returns `"off"` rather than `"none"`. A gate status that treats any tier other than `"none"` as independent evidence will therefore count a self-review; the one shared independence check does not enforce the hard floor at the `off` level.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/gates/reviewers.py:independence_tier

chunk_findings.detail: The note says “the legacy `reviewer_family_must_differ = false` still means off,” but the underlying `independence_level` logic (previous finding #11, untriaged) returns `"family"` whenever `[agent] reviewer_independence == "family"`, even if the legacy boolean is `false`. An org-locked family project that follows this note and keeps its legacy `false` will therefore still get strict family enforcement, not `off`. The text should say the new knob takes precedence, or the implementation must actually honor the legacy false.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/upgrade/unreleased/knob_added.agent.reviewer_independence.toml:8

chunk_findings.detail: The test records a critic passed with evidence model `claude-opus-5` (the author’s own model), sets `cfg.agent.reviewer_family_must_differ = False`, and asserts `_tier(log, cfg)[0] == "off"`. This bakes in the still-unfixed behavior from previous finding 6: `independence_tier` returns `"off"` before checking author identity, so the author’s own model is treated as a usable review when the legacy boolean disables independence. The operator clarification’s hard floor is unconditional—the author’s own model never counts—so this same-model review must yield `"none"`/unavailable. The test should expect `"none"`, not `"off"`.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_reviewer_independence_soft.py:test_off_and_the_legacy_boolean
